fields.v: Not prescribed as a method. Evaluation flow: (1) develop in one persistent builder session: submit snapshots, run on development cases, receive scores and summarized feedback, revise, within time/submission budgets; (2) freeze the delivery (Creation: final workspace; Editing: last accepted submission; Optimization: best accepted dev candidate); (3) held-out execution in an isolated pinned runtime through a fixed model gateway; (4) scoring by validity gates then rubric judge, or native evaluator for Optimization

Acceptance: held-out cases hidden from the builder, validity gates plus rubric scored by an LLM judge (Creation, Editing) or native benchmark evaluator (Optimization). Repetitions: main and harness studies one build per pairing; Lite and ablations three independent builds per condition. Human intervention: none during builds

fields.v: Best on Creation DeepSeek-V4-Pro (19.1, yet below 20 on 8 of 10 tasks); Editing GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro 31.6; Optimization no builder closes more than 5% of the gap on average (13 of 25 runs above starter, 9 below, 3 equal; sign test significant in 5 runs: 3 BrowseComp gains, 2 losses). Creation runs ending development at ≥90 average 9.9 on held-out; Optimization candidates gain 13.1 on development vs 1.8 held-out. Harness matters with model fixed (GPT-5.5 PDF 21.8 Codex vs 42.8 OpenCode; DS-V4-Flash 5.8 Claude Code vs 30.5 DSH); no harness leads for every model. Two development cases raise Result by 34.3 (PDF) and 29.3 (PPTX) over zero; Strategy A lowers PPTX 29.6 → 7.4, Strategy B raises PDF 39.2 → 48.9 'within run-to-run variation'. No significance tests between builders

fields.v: Distinguished builders only partly: all score low and differences are task-specific; held-out testing exposed the development/held-out gap the benchmark targets. Repeatability limited: builds of the same pairing vary widely (GPT-5.6 Sol 32.8, 33.3, 90.5 on DeepTutor; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 0.0, 33.3, 56.8 on repository repair); starter-score SD across repeated evaluation 4.5 (τ3) to 20.8 (PinchBench). Limitations stated by the authors: single build per pairing in main and harness studies; LLM judge errors and judge sharing a model family with builders; levels not comparable across families or studies

fields.v: Limitations: main and harness studies build each pairing once; native Optimization objectives vary between repeated evaluations; Creation/Editing scores inherit model-judge errors, judge shares a model family with at least one builder; one runtime model and judge per family, so levels are not comparable across families; condition studies compared only within themselves. Gaps / future work: harnesses that test against the requirement and verify completion claims; training that rewards behaviour on unseen cases
